sentences.text:
The petitioners, vide the present petition under Article 226 of The Constitution of India read with Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, seek quashing of FIR No.0656/2022 dated 24.12.2022 registered under Section(s) 498A/406/506/34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 at PS.:
Kanjhawala, District Rohini, Delhi and all proceedings emanating therefrom in view of the Settlement Agreement dated 01.09.2023 arrived at between the parties.

2. This petition is accompanied by the Settlement Agreement dated 01.09.2023 and is also supported by affidavits of all the petitioners and of respondent no.2, alongwith proofs of their respective I.Ds.
This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 20/12/2023 at 01:12:03 3.
Petitioner nos. 1 to 12 and as also respondent no.2 are present in Court and have been identified by the IO.
Their credentials have been verified by this Court.
4. Issue Notice.
5. Learned ASC accepts notice.
He confirms that he has no objection to the quashing of the FIR.
6. Learned counsel for the respondent no.2 also accepts notice.
Respondent no.2 confirms that the petitioner no.1 and respondent no.2 have been granted divorce by mutual consent vide Decree of Divorce dated 30.11.2023.

She further affirms the Settlement Agreement dated 01.09.2023 whereby Tarun & Ors vs The State & Anr on 18 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/192942912/
